stem: At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?

choices.text: Dispense because the six-month period remains open after documenting whether the federal five-refill cap had not also been reached.
The five-refill maximum is exhausted even though the six-month period has not ended.
Treat five completed refills as five new prescriptions.
Add a refill after confirming stable therapy with the patient.
Apply the no-refill rule used for Schedule II drugs.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'The five-refill maximum is exhausted even though the six-month period has not ended.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Dispense because the six-month period remains open.' would require that the federal five-refill cap had not also been reached. The decisive cue appears in 'At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Dispense because the six-month period remains open.' would apply only if the federal five-refill cap had not also been reached; 'At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'The five-refill maximum is exhausted even though the six-month period has not ended.': supported by schedule iii-iv refills.
choice_analysis.C: 'Treat five completed refills as five new prescriptions.' would apply only if each refill carried independent refill authority; 'At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Add a refill after confirming stable therapy with the patient.' would apply only if a pharmacist could renew Schedule IV authorization without the practitioner; 'At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Apply the no-refill rule used for Schedule II drugs.' would apply only if triazolam were Schedule II rather than Schedule IV; 'At prescription intake, a Halcion prescription is five months old and has five completed refills. Which fact is dispositive?' states otherwise.

related_facts: triazolam (Halcion) is used for short-term treatment of insomnia; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
